content:
Hi-

I've built (with AI assistance) a pipeline for translating large math PDFs to verso. My hope is that this could be part of a large-scale autoformalization pipeline (like AutoFormBot) for turning mass quantities of tokens into formalized results.

Here's the code: https://github.com/phulin/textbook. It uses Baidu's very generous free-tier OCR model to do a first pass, and then does a validation pass with Codex or Claude.

I know this is not really the Mathlib approach, and that's fine, I would expect this to be more useful for Lean Pool-style projects. I am new to the community and don't want to step any toes. My instinct is that it would be useful to start building up a library of formalized subfields - e.g. in FLT such an effort could start making progress towards the knownIn1980s results.

Great effort, we are currently improving the AutoformBot: see https://github.com/VivienCabannes/autoform-bot, and are testing it for some formalization projects, see #AI authored projects > Besov spaces via Littlewood–Paley theory. I would love to sync so that we can consolidate the tools that people wants to use into a community plugin
Oh, very cool! Let me know how I can help.
